question: Who usually acts as the main communication link for the home health team?

options.A: The family pet owner
options.B: The patient's insurance case manager
options.C: The local pharmacist
options.D: The primary home health nurse

explanation: You are the captain of the ship! The primary nurse coordinates visits, gathers updates from other therapists, and updates the doctor.

question: What communication tool helps nurses pass structured and concise patient or situation data during a crisis?

options.A: Casual text messages sent without checking details
options.B: SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation)
options.C: Complex medical research articles from foreign journals
options.D: Long narrative diary entries written at the end of the shift

explanation: SBAR gives healthcare workers a quick, organized way to share essential facts without wasting time during emergencies. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h6)

question: Why is the moving ambulance considered a difficult environment for clinical assessments?

options.A: Patients are always unconscious and unable to speak during transit
options.B: Medical equipment completely stops working inside motorized vehicles
options.C: Vibration, road noise, and cramped space interfere with standard checks
options.D: Natural lighting makes it impossible to see skin color changes

explanation: Motion, noise, and physical constraints make hearing breath sounds or palpating faint pulses much harder than in a quiet hospital bed. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h1)

question: A nurse is preparing to send a patient home for the weekend. What is the most important action regarding medications?

options.A: Ensuring the correct medication supply is packaged with clear instructions for the family
options.B: Telling the patient to stop all medications for the weekend break
options.C: Asking the family to buy medications from an unregistered market
options.D: Hiding the medication supply in the suitcase without telling anyone

explanation: Clear labels and proper medication supplies prevent missed doses and keep the patient safe and stable all weekend long.

question: Which of these is NOT a good self-care practice for managing long-term leg swelling?

options.A: Wearing tight, restrictive garters to keep the swelling squeezed down
options.B: Elevating the legs periodically throughout the day
options.C: Following a reduced-sodium diet as prescribed by the doctor
options.D: Inspecting the lower legs daily for any skin breaks or redness

explanation: Spot on! Avoid tight bands or restrictive garters because they actually choke off circulation and make fluid pooling worse. Proper medical compression stockings should be used instead!

question: What is the main characteristic of a democratic leadership style?

options.A: Focus only on financial transactions
options.B: Shared decision-making and team input
options.C: Complete freedom given to junior staff
options.D: Strict rules with no room for discussion

explanation: Democratic leaders actively seek the opinions and ideas of their team members before making decisions. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is a common mistake that can make small changes on a line graph look way bigger than they actually are?

options.A: Starting the vertical axis at a number other than zero without a break symbol
options.B: Placing the time variable on the horizontal axis
options.C: Including a clear legend for multiple lines
options.D: Using a straight ruler to connect the individual data points

explanation: You got it! Messing with the bottom of the vertical axis stretches the slope and can trick the eye into seeing a crisis where there isn't one.

question: Why does a severe opioid overdose lead to dangerous breathing problems?

options.A: It causes immediate physical swelling and closure of the main vocal cords
options.B: It depresses the respiratory control center in the brainstem, reducing breathing rate
options.C: It freezes the movement of the diaphragm muscle by destroying motor nerves
options.D: It triggers severe allergic bronchospasm in the small bronchial airways

explanation: Opioids affect the part of the brain that tells the body to breathe, causing breathing to slow down and eventually stop if untreated.

question: A ward successfully tested a new handoff communication checklist with one nurse for a week. What is the most logical next step?

options.A: Immediately fire all staff who refuse to use the old checklist
options.B: Expand the test to include all nurses on that specific shift for another week
options.C: Abandon the checklist because testing is now complete
options.D: Mandate the checklist for every hospital in the entire country immediately

explanation: You nailed it! Scaling up should happen step-by-step—moving from one person to a small group before trying a wider rollout.

question: What makes the intramuscular route absorb medications faster than the subcutaneous route?

options.A: Muscles have a richer blood supply than fat tissue
options.B: Subcutaneous fat repels liquid medications
options.C: Muscle tissue contains more nerve endings
options.D: Injections go straight into the main arteries

explanation: Skeletal muscle has a dense network of blood vessels that quickly take up and distribute injected medications compared to fatty layers. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h1)

question: What is the primary function of neuroglial cells?

options.A: To support, insulate, and protect neurons
options.B: To produce hormones for the endocrine system
options.C: To generate electrical impulses for muscle contraction
options.D: To carry sensory messages directly to the cerebral cortex

explanation: Neuroglia act as supportive cells that nourish and protect delicate neurons in the nervous system. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h5)

question: A nurse is teaching a rural community about cholera prevention. Which approach will work best?

options.A: Insisting that villagers change their ancient cultural practices without any explanation
options.B: Handing out complex scientific research journals written in advanced medical terminology
options.C: Waiting until an outbreak kills several people before holding a public meeting
options.D: Using local languages and culturally relevant examples to explain safe drinking water habits

explanation: Spot on! Keeping health education simple, friendly, and in the local language ensures everyone understands and can easily protect themselves.

question: What is the main goal of performing medication reconciliation?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of hospital pharmacy supplies
options.B: To test the memory of newly graduated nursing students
options.C: To avoid errors like missed doses, double dosing, and clashes
options.D: To force patients to buy their medications from the hospital

explanation: The core purpose is to catch and stop mistakes early, keeping your patient safe from harmful drug clashes. You're building solid clinical instincts!

question: What is the main reason nurses use quick screening tools like the CAGE questionnaire?

options.A: To measure the exact level of vitamins present in the bloodstream
options.B: To quickly identify potential substance abuse or dependence problems
options.C: To calculate the correct dosage of emergency antidote medication
options.D: To diagnose specific mental health disorders like major depression

explanation: Exactly! Screening tools are short, easy-to-use questions that help us spot patients who might need a closer look or professional support for substance use.

question: What does 'primary hypertension' mean?

options.A: High blood pressure with no single identifiable medical cause
options.B: Blood pressure that only affects young children and infants
options.C: High blood pressure caused by a single known kidney disease
options.D: A temporary spike in pressure caused by severe acute stress

explanation: Exactly! Primary (or essential) hypertension develops gradually over time without one specific underlying medical trigger.

question: A patient with advanced cervical cancer comes in with a swollen right leg and dull flank pain. What is the most likely reason for this?

options.A: Metastatic spread of cancer cells to the bones of the foot
options.B: Tumor compression of pelvic veins and the ureter
options.C: Development of deep vein thrombosis from excessive physical activity
options.D: Severe systemic dehydration caused by heavy vaginal bleeding

explanation: Makes sense when you picture it: a growing tumor in the pelvis can press against nearby blood vessels (causing leg swelling) and block the tubes leading from the kidneys, known as the ureters (causing flank pain).

question: A pregnant woman in a low-income community skips her antenatal visits to buy food for her children. What economic factor is primarily driving her decision?

options.A: Macroeconomic surplus
options.B: Out-of-pocket financial barrier
options.C: Brain drain
options.D: Excess health insurance coverage

explanation: Having to choose between basic survival needs like food and paying for medical care highlights the harsh impact of direct out-of-pocket expenses. [learn more](GST322_U3_T7#GST322_U3_T7_h5)

question: An asthma patient says they need to use their rescue inhaler every single day for wheezing. What does this tell you?

options.A: The patient is experiencing a normal, expected reaction to therapy
options.B: The spacer device is broken and needs to be replaced immediately
options.C: The patient is using the correct technique for daily maintenance
options.D: The underlying disease is poorly controlled and needs medical review

explanation: Needing a rescue inhaler more than twice a week is a red flag that the asthma isn't well-controlled, meaning the doctor needs to review their daily maintenance plan.

question: Why is it important for modern nurses to get comfortable using bedside technology?

options.A: It shapes every shift and helps protect patients from human error
options.B: Patients refuse care unless digital devices are present
options.C: It completely replaces the need to perform physical assessments
options.D: Hospital accreditation depends entirely on computer typing speed

explanation: You got it! Smart tools are part of daily clinical life, and they act as a safety net to catch mistakes before they hurt anyone.

question: How would you describe a direct cost in patient care?

options.A: An unexpected emergency expense covered by insurance
options.B: The overall electricity bill for the entire hospital building
options.C: An expense easily traced to a specific patient or unit
options.D: A hidden fee charged by hospital administrators

explanation: Direct costs point straight to one specific place or person—like the exact medication or supplies given to a particular patient. Simple and clear!

question: A patient suddenly loses their voice and sounds very hoarse after a cold. Which part of the airway is likely inflamed?

options.A: The palatine tonsils
options.B: The nasal cavity
options.C: The larynx
options.D: The frontal sinuses

explanation: Well done! The larynx is your voice box, so when it gets inflamed (laryngitis), your vocal cords swell and your voice gets raspy.

question: What is the main energy source that crosses the placenta to feed the growing fetus?

options.A: Lactic acid
options.B: Glucose
options.C: Fatty acids
options.D: Protein

explanation: Glucose is the baby's main fuel! It crosses the placenta quickly via facilitated diffusion to keep up with high energy demands. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h5)

question: What exactly are parasitic ova?

options.A: The eggs produced by parasitic worms
options.B: Toxic metabolic waste products of bacteria
options.C: The larval stage of protozoan parasites
options.D: Immature fungal spores found in soil

explanation: Think of ova simply as the reproductive eggs laid by helminths (parasitic worms). Spot on! You've got this.

question: Which of these actions is WRONG when monitoring a client's nutritional progress?

options.A: Checking regular weight trends over time
options.B: Ignoring client feedback on food preferences
options.C: Documenting specific physical measurements
options.D: Reviewing the client's recent food diaries

explanation: Never ignore what the client likes! Diet plans only work if they fit the client's personal lifestyle and taste.

question: What is a common misunderstanding about what local disaster agencies do?

options.A: Many believe local agencies possess more aircraft than the national air force
options.B: Citizens assume local agencies are solely responsible for national monetary policy
options.C: People often think they only distribute relief materials after a crisis rather than focusing on prevention
options.D: It is widely assumed that local agencies manage international trade agreements

explanation: Exactly! While handing out relief is the part we see most, good local agencies actually put huge effort into stopping disasters before they happen.

question: What is the medical term for inflammation of the urinary bladder, often caused by a bacterial infection?

options.A: Pyelitis
options.B: Urethritis
options.C: Cystitis
options.D: Nephritis

explanation: Cystitis refers specifically to inflammation of the bladder lining, frequently resulting from a bacterial urinary tract infection. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T3#GNS121_U2_T3_h6)

question: What should a nurse use when counselling a patient who does not speak the local language?

options.A: A noisy hospital hallway speaker
options.B: A complex English pharmacology textbook
options.C: A professional medical interpreter
options.D: A young child visiting the family

explanation: Professional interpreters ensure accurate translation of critical medical concepts while keeping patient information private and secure.

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of a vulvovaginal yeast infection (candidiasis)?

options.A: Yellow-green, frothy discharge with strawberry spots
options.B: Thick, white, cottage-cheese-like discharge with intense itching
options.C: Thin, gray-white discharge with a strong fishy odor
options.D: Clear, watery discharge with severe lower abdominal pain

explanation: Spot on! Yeast infections are famous for that thick, white discharge and relentless itching, without a fishy smell. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h4)

question: What is the main job of the skin as a body organ?

options.A: Filtering waste products directly from the bloodstream
options.B: Regulating the production of major digestive enzymes
options.C: Serving as a primary defense against pathogens and fluid loss
options.D: Producing red blood cells for systemic circulation

explanation: Great job! Think of your skin as your body's natural raincoat and security guard rolled into one—it keeps germs out and your precious body fluids in.

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of chronic osteomyelitis?

options.A: Instantaneous paralysis of the affected limb
options.B: A sudden high fever with no local pain whatsoever
options.C: Complete numbness and coldness in the toes
options.D: A draining sinus tract leaking pus onto the skin

explanation: A sinus tract is a little tunnel that forms from the infected bone out to the skin, constantly draining pus. A classic clinical clue!

question: What is the primary purpose of client rights in a healthcare setting?

options.A: To ensure that doctors have absolute authority over treatment choices
options.B: To reduce the financial operating costs of running a public hospital
options.C: To give the nursing staff total control over daily ward routines
options.D: To protect the personal dignity and autonomy of the patient

explanation: Client rights exist primarily to safeguard the patient's individual worth and decision-making power while receiving medical care. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h1)

question: What is the main goal of preventive reproductive health services?

options.A: To treat infertility using modern assisted reproductive technology
options.B: To cure advanced stages of reproductive tract cancers
options.C: To stop health problems before they start through screening and education
options.D: To manage high-risk surgical emergencies in labor wards

explanation: Preventive services aim to intercept diseases early or stop them entirely using vaccines, screenings, and education. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h2)

question: What does noticeable muscle wasting in the temples and shoulders suggest about a patient?

options.A: Long-standing protein-calorie malnutrition
options.B: Normal aging with no clinical significance
options.C: Excessive intake of dietary carbohydrates
options.D: Temporary dehydration from lack of water

explanation: When the body lacks sufficient protein and calories over time, it breaks down muscle mass for energy, leading to visible wasting in areas like the temples and shoulders. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h6)

question: An instructor gives you tips on your sterile technique halfway through your ward posting so you can fix your mistakes. What kind of evaluation is this?

options.A: Affective evaluation
options.B: Norm-referenced evaluation
options.C: Summative evaluation
options.D: Formative evaluation

explanation: That's a formative evaluation! Getting guidance while you are still learning helps you improve on the spot. You're building solid clinical habits.

question: Why do traditional beliefs often blame ancestral displeasure for psychological distress?

options.A: To show that physical injuries cause all brain disorders
options.B: To discourage individuals from talking to their neighbors
options.C: To prove that modern science has all the correct answers
options.D: To encourage people to maintain family traditions and moral codes

explanation: Makes total sense! Attributing illness to broken taboos or ancestral anger reinforces community morality and the importance of heritage.

question: How do computers help nurses manage vital signs and patient numbers?

options.A: By following programmed steps to turn raw numbers into useful information
options.B: By making independent medical diagnoses using intuition
options.C: By storing information permanently without electricity
options.D: By turning handwritten notes into paper charts

explanation: Computers don't think like humans do! They rely on smart programming to turn raw numbers into clear, meaningful information for your shift.

question: Which nursing practice is a great example of direct cost containment?

options.A: Refusing to admit patients who lack private health insurance
options.B: Turning off lights in patient rooms when natural sunlight is available
options.C: Avoiding the hoarding of unused sterile supplies in unit cupboards
options.D: Canceling all staff training sessions to save on travel allowances

explanation: Not hoarding supplies stops items from expiring on shelves and reduces waste. Small daily habits make a huge difference!

question: Which type of hospital waste must always be destroyed using high-temperature incineration?

options.A: Anatomical and pathological waste
options.B: Used office paper and administrative files
options.C: Non-contaminated cardboard delivery boxes
options.D: Empty intravenous fluid glass bottles

explanation: Human tissues and body parts must be completely incinerated for sanitary and cultural reasons. You're building great clinical habits!

question: Why is it helpful to know the boundaries of a healthcare system?

options.A: To prevent patients from ever leaving the hospital premises
options.B: To restrict communication between different hospital departments
options.C: To calculate the exact profit margins of the facility each month
options.D: To know what is within direct control versus external factors

explanation: Boundaries help us figure out what we can directly manage on our ward versus what requires help from outside. It saves you so much stress when you know your scope!

question: What does the catchy phrase U=U mean in modern HIV care?

options.A: Urinary excretion of unabsorbed medication
options.B: Unprotected union under treatment
options.C: Universal use of universal precautions
options.D: Undetectable equals untransmittable

explanation: Brilliant! U=U means when a person's viral load is undetectable through ART, they cannot sexually pass the virus to others.

question: Which home health team member specializes in treating swallowing disorders and speech difficulties?

options.A: Speech-language pathologist
options.B: Physical therapist
options.C: Occupational therapist
options.D: Licensed practical nurse

explanation: Speech therapists assess and treat patients who have trouble speaking, understanding language, or swallowing safely. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why do modern nurses need to understand a bit of health economics?

options.A: To calculate daily patient medication dosages
options.B: To purchase personal medical equipment
options.C: To prove the financial value of professional care
options.D: To manage hospital pharmacy inventories

explanation: Knowing a bit of economics helps you stand up for your ward, justify why you need more hands on deck, and show management how vital nursing really is.

question: Which body is directly responsible for regulating nursing training and practice here in Nigeria?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.B: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.C: Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare
options.D: National Universities Commission

explanation: That's the NMCN! They are our main body, setting the rules and standards for all nursing schools and practice across the country.

question: What must be done immediately after collecting raw data from a community survey?

options.A: Dismissal of all community health committees
options.B: Immediate closure of all local markets
options.C: Destruction of the completed questionnaires
options.D: Data analysis and tabulation

explanation: Collected data must be sorted and analyzed to reveal patterns, rates, and actual health needs before planning interventions. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why is it important for nurses in Nigeria to ask patients about any traditional herbal remedies they might be taking?

options.A: Traditional herbs are scientifically proven to cure type 1 diabetes permanently
options.B: Herbal products completely replace the need for blood glucose monitoring
options.C: Traditional remedies have no chemical impact on human liver enzymes
options.D: Herbal mixtures can interact with prescribed drugs and cause unexpected blood sugar drops

explanation: Spot on! Many local herbal preparations can unexpectedly drop blood sugar levels, leading to severe hypoglycaemia when mixed with regular diabetes medications.

question: What makes treating fungal infections in patients particularly tricky for doctors and nurses?

options.A: Fungi do not have cell membranes to target with drugs
options.B: Fungal cells are eukaryotic and share similarities with human cells
options.C: Fungi change their shape too quickly for laboratory identification
options.D: Antifungal medications only work if the patient has a high fever

explanation: Because fungi share similar cell structures with us humans, strong drugs that kill fungus can sometimes accidentally harm human cells too, leading to more side effects.

question: What is another name commonly given to the enteric nervous system?

options.A: The central coordinator
options.B: The second brain
options.C: The vagal network
options.D: The sympathetic trunk

explanation: The enteric nervous system is often called the second brain because it contains a vast network of neurons that can control digestive functions independently of the brain. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T12#GNS121_U1_T12_h1)

question: Why is male involvement important in family planning decisions?

options.A: It reduces the cost of buying medications
options.B: It gives men total control over family size
options.C: It removes the need for female contraceptive use
options.D: It ensures joint agreement and supports birth spacing

explanation: Family planning works best when both partners discuss and agree on methods that protect the health of the mother. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h4)

question: Where does Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) fit into the safety hierarchy for handling workplace hazards?

options.A: It is the last line of defense after other controls
options.B: It is only required after a toxic exposure has occurred
options.C: It replaces the need for proper chemical labelling
options.D: It is the primary method to eliminate workplace hazards

explanation: That's correct! PPE depends entirely on human behavior and proper wear, making it our last safety net if other controls fail. We always prefer removing the danger first.

question: A 16-year-old girl drops out of school due to an unplanned pregnancy. What long-term impact is she most likely to face?

options.A: Immediate government employment
options.B: Automatic university admission
options.C: Lifelong economic hardship
options.D: Complete immunity from malaria

explanation: Interrupting education early often limits future career opportunities, leading to long-term financial struggles. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h2)

question: How does having a daily work schedule help a client dealing with auditory hallucinations?

options.A: It replaces the need for any psychiatric evaluation
options.B: It blocks all sound waves from entering the ears
options.C: It completely cures the brain of abnormal electrical impulses
options.D: It provides a healthy distraction from distressing symptoms

explanation: When clients are busy focusing on work tasks, they have less time to dwell on troubling internal voices. You're doing great!

question: Which of these actions breaks patient data privacy rules in a digital hospital?

options.A: Sharing your computer login password with a fellow nurse who forgot theirs
options.B: Discussing a client's lab results inside a private consultation room
options.C: Reviewing the medical history of an assigned client during your shift
options.D: Logging out of the electronic health record workstation before walking away

explanation: Never share your password! If someone else uses your login, you are responsible for any changes made in that patient's file. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h6)

question: Which option is NOT possible when assessing a patient during a strictly voice-only phone call?

options.A: Asking direct questions about pain level and location
options.B: Listening carefully to changes in the patient's breathing sound
options.C: Observing skin color changes directly through the phone screen
options.D: Evaluating the tone of voice and hesitation in speech

explanation: Spot on! An ordinary phone call transmits sound, not video. You can hear their breathing or tone of voice, but you cannot see if their skin is pale or jaundiced.

question: What communication style works best to encourage a patient to adopt healthier eating habits?

options.A: A silent demonstration with no words
options.B: A strict and formal medical lecture
options.C: A rapid list of commands to follow
options.D: A collaborative and supportive dialogue

explanation: Working together through supportive conversation helps patients feel empowered rather than judged or forced. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T20#GNS214_U1_T20_h4)

question: What is a major advantage of open-access academic journals?

options.A: Articles are published overnight without any editorial oversight
options.B: Practitioners worldwide can read the findings without paying expensive fees
options.C: Studies are automatically approved for funding by the health ministry
options.D: Researchers never have to revise their original drafts or fix errors

explanation: Open-access removes paywalls so that nurses and the public can freely access vital health information. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h2)

question: What kind of special precautions do you need when caring for a patient with active pulmonary tuberculosis?

options.A: Contact precautions
options.B: Airborne precautions
options.C: Droplet precautions
options.D: Standard precautions only

explanation: Spot on! TB germs float around in tiny particles in the air, so you'll need specialised protection like an N95 respirator mask.

question: What is a major error a nurse can make during community mobilisation?

options.A: Asking local leaders for permission to enter the village
options.B: Taking over leadership and making decisions for the community
options.C: Teaching mothers how to prepare oral rehydration salt
options.D: Working with local volunteers to clean up the environment

explanation: Nurses should facilitate and empower, not take control and rob the community of their self-reliance. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting a clinical audit in a reproductive health unit?

options.A: To increase the amount of financial profit the hospital makes
options.B: To find staff members to fire after an adverse event happens
options.C: To compare actual patient outcomes and care against established standards
options.D: To reduce the number of medical records kept in the filing room

explanation: Correct! Clinical audits help us look at our current care practices, spot gaps, and find ways to improve our nursing service.

question: Which feature is essential for a central health care waste storage room?

options.A: Carpeted flooring for noise reduction
options.B: Large glass windows for direct sunlight exposure
options.C: Open access for patients and visitors
options.D: Secure locks to prevent unauthorized entry

explanation: Central storage areas must be locked securely to keep unauthorized persons, scavengers, and animals away from hazardous materials. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h4)

question: Which part of a draped instrument table is officially considered sterile?

options.A: The top surface and everything hanging below the edge
options.B: Only the flat top surface level with the table
options.C: The entire table including the legs and wheels
options.D: Only the center portion where heavy trays sit

explanation: Remember the golden rule: anything hanging below the tabletop edge is out of sight and out of the sterile zone!

question: An environmental health officer is checking a suspected food poisoning outbreak at a local canteen. What is the very first step before any lab testing can start?

options.A: Collecting a representative sample using sterile equipment and proper cold storage
options.B: Immediately closing down all food businesses operating in that neighborhood
options.C: Administering intravenous antibiotics to all customers who ate at the canteen
options.D: Spraying chemical disinfectants across the entire kitchen and dining area

explanation: Brilliant! Lab tests are only as good as the sample you send them. Proper sterile collection and keeping it cold are always step one.

question: What is the main goal of a peer support program for second victims?

options.A: To find grounds for disciplinary action or termination
options.B: To re-test the nurse's clinical skills in a simulation lab
options.C: To conduct a legal investigation of the nurse's actions
options.D: To provide a confidential space to talk with trained colleagues

explanation: Sometimes you just need someone who truly understands the hospital ward stress to listen without judging. Peer support is all about healing together!

question: What is the main goal of medication reconciliation?

options.A: To destroy any expired herbal remedies found inside the patient's home
options.B: To calculate the total financial cost of treatment for the hospital billing department
options.C: To create an accurate, complete list of all drugs a patient is taking across transitions of care
options.D: To force the patient to buy all their medications from the hospital pharmacy

explanation: Medication reconciliation is like making a master list. Whenever a patient moves from home to the ward (or ward to discharge), we check every single drug they are taking to prevent mistakes.

question: Why do food workers in Nigeria need a mandatory medical certificate?

options.A: To prove they are free from infectious diseases before handling food
options.B: To test how well they can cook local dishes
options.C: To help local government offices generate revenue
options.D: To figure out the right salary level for kitchen staff

explanation: Medical checks ensure that kitchen staff aren't carrying hidden infections that could easily spread to the meals they prepare.

question: What must happen before a public sector nurse moves from probation to a permanent staff member?

options.A: Direct purchase of a permanent tenure certificate from the ministry
options.B: Automatic time elapsed without any evaluation of clinical skills required
options.C: Satisfactory completion of the probation period and positive supervisor evaluations
options.D: Completion of mandatory political party membership registration

explanation: To get confirmed permanently, you need to spend the required time on the job and get good reviews from your supervisors.

question: How does chronic psychological stress typically affect food cravings?

options.A: It increases a natural desire for raw vegetables and water
options.B: It raises cortisol and triggers cravings for fatty, sugary foods
options.C: It forces the digestive system to absorb fewer total calories
options.D: It completely stops the body from digesting any proteins

explanation: You got it! High cortisol from stress tricks the brain into seeking out dense, comforting, high-calorie foods for quick energy.

question: When is a pie chart the best choice for showing your data?

options.A: When showing parts of a single whole
options.B: When tracking patient recovery trends daily
options.C: When measuring the correlation of two variables
options.D: When comparing exact values across time

explanation: Spot on! Pie charts are brilliant when you want to show how different pieces fit together to make one complete whole.

question: What is the boundary line that separates the false pelvis from the true pelvis?

options.A: Pelvic brim
options.B: Sacral promontory
options.C: Pubic symphysis
options.D: Ischial spine

explanation: Think of the pelvic brim as the dividing line sitting right between the upper false pelvis and the lower true pelvis.

question: A nurse does the spatula test on a baby suspected of having tetanus. What reaction confirms the diagnosis?

options.A: The infant sneezes and turns the head away
options.B: The infant opens the mouth wider to yawn
options.C: The infant bites down tightly on the spatula
options.D: The infant immediately vomits clear mucus

explanation: Correct! Instead of a normal gag reflex, touching the back of the throat with a spatula causes a tetanus baby to bite down tightly due to reflex spasms.

question: A client returns complaining of annoying, continuous spotting two months after her implant insertion. What is your best first nursing action?

options.A: Insist that she has an undiagnosed infection and prescribe strong broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: Validate her experience, explain that irregular bleeding is a known side effect, and offer treatment options
options.C: Tell her the implant is defective and demand that she undergo immediate emergency surgery
options.D: Advise her to stop drinking water for three days to dry up her internal hormonal secretions

explanation: Always listen with empathy! Reassuring her that spotting is normal and offering management options helps her feel supported and confident.

question: Why should you use the flat palms of your hands instead of your fingertips when shaping a wet cast?

options.A: Fingertips leave indentations that can press into skin and cause pressure sores
options.B: Palms generate friction heat that helps the plaster harden more evenly
options.C: Palms allow the nurse to apply much tighter circumferential pressure
options.D: Using fingertips makes the outer surface of the cast too rough and abrasive

explanation: Finger pressure creates dents inside the cast that can pinch the patient's skin and cut off good blood flow.

question: What is a great food tip for a mum dealing with early morning sickness?

options.A: Consuming a large, high-fat breakfast immediately upon waking
options.B: Drinking two large glasses of citrus juice on an empty stomach
options.C: Eating small, dry carbohydrate snacks like crackers before getting out of bed
options.D: Restricting all fluid intake throughout the entire day

explanation: Dry snacks help settle a restless morning tummy and gently boost blood sugar without triggering nausea.

question: As a student nurse, what should you tell someone who asks if the mother's blood and the baby's blood mix directly?

options.A: No, because maternal blood never enters the placenta at all.
options.B: No, they are separated by a thin placental membrane that prevents direct contact.
options.C: Yes, but only during the first trimester before the villi mature.
options.D: Yes, they mix freely in the intervillous space to maximize oxygen delivery.

explanation: A common exam favorite! Mother and baby blood streams never actually mix; they stay safely separated by a thin membrane while trading oxygen and nutrients across.

question: Why must a nurse know the exact landmarks of the vulva?

options.A: To pass a urinary catheter without missing the urethra
options.B: To prevent ovarian cysts
options.C: To measure blood pressure correctly
options.D: To track the exact day of ovulation

explanation: Spot on! Knowing your anatomy keeps procedures safe and stops you from accidentally placing a catheter into the vaginal opening instead of the urethra.

question: Why is keeping furniture in the same place important for someone with low vision?

options.A: It prevents dust from accumulating under heavy chairs
options.B: It ensures compliance with local fire safety regulations
options.C: It improves natural lighting inside the living space
options.D: It helps them navigate safely using their memory of the layout

explanation: When furniture stays put, individuals can use their memory of the room to walk around safely without bumping into unexpected obstacles.

question: Why do different agencies need to work together during a disaster response?

options.A: It gives nurses the authority to write new national laws
options.B: It replaces the need for community education and local drills
options.C: It guarantees that natural hazards will completely miss the country
options.D: It ensures that different groups do not duplicate efforts and waste resources

explanation: Brilliant! Sharing information and working hand-in-hand prevents confusion and keeps help running smoothly.

question: What is the main antiviral drug used to treat Lassa fever?

options.A: Chloroquine
options.B: Ribavirin
options.C: Artemether
options.D: Acyclovir

explanation: Ribavirin is the go-to antiviral. When given early, it drastically lowers the severity of the illness and saves lives.

question: What is the main difference between equality and equity in primary health care delivery?

options.A: Equity gives extra resources to those with greater needs
options.B: Equality prohibits the treatment of wealthy patients
options.C: Equality means spending the exact same amount of money on every hospital
options.D: Equity focuses solely on urban populations

explanation: Equity is about fairness, meaning vulnerable groups get the extra support they need to reach the same health outcomes as others. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why do nurses and doctors use a standard classification system for FGM?

options.A: To help healthcare workers document and assess clinical needs
options.B: To assign legal penalties to specific practitioners
options.C: To determine the correct surgical reversal technique
options.D: To calculate the financial cost of hospital treatment

explanation: Exactly! Knowing the specific type helps nurses understand the patient's history and plan the best, most sensitive care possible.

question: What is the main reason a multidisciplinary team is essential in CBR?

options.A: Clients have diverse physical, psychological, social, and economic needs that one profession cannot cover alone
options.B: Government policies fine clinics that operate with only one nurse
options.C: Hospitals have too many idle workers who need field assignments
options.D: It stops professionals from arguing about who is in charge of the clinic

explanation: Recovery involves medical, social, and financial dimensions, requiring nurses, social workers, and trainers to combine their unique skills. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary role of water inside the human body?

options.A: Stimulating the production of red blood cells
options.B: Providing a dense reserve of long-term energy
options.C: Serving as the medium for all metabolic reactions
options.D: Preventing the breakdown of dietary proteins

explanation: Water provides the fluid environment where nutrients, wastes, and chemical reactions take place continuously. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h4)

question: Which nursing action is an example of primary prevention?

options.A: Checking blood pressure at a community health fair
options.B: Teaching foot care to a patient with diabetes
options.C: Providing cardiac rehabilitation after a heart attack
options.D: Administering a routine measles vaccine to a child

explanation: Vaccines stop a disease from occurring in the first place, which is the definition of primary prevention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a main cause of peptic ulcers?

options.A: Prolonged use of NSAID medications
options.B: High dietary salt intake alone
options.C: Excessive gastric acid production
options.D: Helicobacter pylori infection

explanation: While spicy or salty foods can irritate an existing ulcer, they don't cause them on their own. Ulcers are mainly caused by H. pylori bacteria and regular use of NSAID painkillers.

question: Why must a nurse wear PPE when performing last offices?

options.A: To protect against exposure to infectious body fluids
options.B: To comply with fire safety rules in the hospital
options.C: To prevent the family from recognizing the nurse later
options.D: To keep the nurse's uniform from getting wrinkled

explanation: Pathogens can still be present in bodily fluids after death, making standard precautions and PPE essential for staff safety. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h3)

question: Why do we use injectable (parenteral) artesunate for severe, complicated malaria instead of oral drugs?

options.A: It achieves rapid systemic drug levels when the child cannot safely swallow
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for nursing monitoring
options.C: It has zero side effects compared to oral tablets
options.D: It cures the infection permanently in a single minute

explanation: When a child is vomiting or too weak to swallow, injections get the life-saving medicine directly into the bloodstream fast. Excellent nursing judgment!

question: A nurse treats a high blood pressure patient living in a neighborhood with poor food access. What is the best all-round approach?

options.A: Provide medication while also connecting the patient to local nutritional resources and food programs
options.B: Focus solely on writing prescriptions without discussing the patient's diet
options.C: Tell the patient to only purchase expensive imported foods from distant supermarkets
options.D: Advise the patient to stop eating entirely until their blood pressure normalizes

explanation: Brilliant nursing care! Good treatment means handing out medicine while also helping the patient find practical food support right in their community.

question: Who is famous for unchaining patients at the Bicêtre Hospital in Paris during the moral treatment era?

options.A: Philippe Pinel
options.B: Dorothea Dix
options.C: Linda Richards
options.D: Sigmund Freud

explanation: Philippe Pinel was a true hero for human rights. He stepped up, took off the chains, and insisted that psychiatric patients deserved respect and dignity.

question: In the '5 As' smoking cessation framework, which step means checking if a patient uses tobacco during every clinic visit?

options.A: Assess
options.B: Advise
options.C: Ask
options.D: Arrange

explanation: The 'Ask' step is simply checking and recording whether every patient uses tobacco. Simple, direct, and essential for good nursing care!

question: Which of these is an example of an internal factor that can affect a person's health?

options.A: Cultural family traditions
options.B: Availability of community hospitals
options.C: Genetic makeup and inherited traits
options.D: Socioeconomic income level

explanation: You've got this! Internal factors come from within us—like our genes, age, and sex—while external factors come from our surroundings.

question: What happens when you take in more food energy (calories) than your body burns off?

options.A: Excess energy is stored primarily as fat
options.B: The body uses up its protein stores completely
options.C: Cellular chemical reactions stop entirely
options.D: Metabolic rate drops permanently to zero

explanation: Think of it like money: if you earn more than you spend, you save the extra! The body packs away extra calories as fat tissue to use for a rainy day.

question: Under Nigerian law, what is a specific rule public organizations must follow regarding employment?

options.A: They must provide free housing for all disabled citizens.
options.B: They must exempt disabled individuals from paying any taxes.
options.C: They must allocate at least 5% of their workforce positions to persons with disabilities.
options.D: They must fund private medical clinics in every rural community.

explanation: The law sets a helpful employment quota requiring public establishments to reserve a minimum of 5% of their jobs for qualified persons with disabilities.

question: A patient is having a sudden panic attack on the ward. What is the best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Telling the patient to stop worrying about nothing
options.B: Guiding the patient through slow, controlled breathing exercises
options.C: Administering a high-dose herbal supplement immediately
options.D: Leaving the patient alone in a quiet room to sleep

explanation: Deep, slow breathing triggers the body's calming system, helping to physically slow down anxiety and panic right away.

question: A family caregiver looks very tired and says they can't sleep because of worry over night medications. What should you do?

options.A: Assess caregiver strain and explore local support or respite options
options.B: Discharge the patient immediately due to unreliable family support
options.C: Advise the patient to manage all nighttime medications alone
options.D: Tell the family member that burnout is simply part of being a caregiver

explanation: You got it! Caregiver fatigue is real. Checking on their well-being and finding support helps keep home care safe and sustainable.

question: According to the Frank-Starling law, what happens when more blood returns to the heart?

options.A: The ventricles stretch more and pump out a stronger stroke volume
options.B: Myocardial oxygen consumption decreases significantly
options.C: The intercalated discs close tightly to prevent over-expansion
options.D: The heart rate drops immediately to allow more filling time

explanation: Think of the heart like a rubber band: the more it stretches as it fills with blood, the stronger it snaps back to pump that blood out!

question: What is the main goal of the controlling function in nursing management?

options.A: Recruiting qualified nursing personnel for open shifts
options.B: Punishing staff members who make clinical documentation errors
options.C: Monitoring activities to ensure they meet established goals
options.D: Creating brand new institutional policies from scratch

explanation: Think of controlling as checking in to make sure your ward's care and daily targets match what the hospital planned to achieve. You're doing great!

question: Which of these is NOT a common trigger for a psychotic episode?

options.A: Using recreational cannabis
options.B: Experiencing severe life stress
options.C: Having a family history of psychosis
options.D: Eating a high-sodium diet

explanation: Spot on! Eating salty food won't cause psychosis, but heavy stress, genetics, and substances like cannabis definitely can.

question: What does a 'feasible' research project mean for a student?

options.A: Whether the hospital will change its name after the study
options.B: Whether the research topic is popular on social media
options.C: How many international awards the study might win
options.D: Whether the study can actually be done with available resources

explanation: Feasibility is just about being realistic—making sure you have enough time, money, and materials to finish the study without burning out.

question: What is the main difference between an epidemic and an endemic disease?

options.A: An epidemic is an unexpected surge above normal levels, while endemic is the expected baseline.
options.B: An endemic condition requires quarantine, whereas an epidemic resolves without treatment.
options.C: An endemic disease spreads worldwide, while an epidemic stays within one local village.
options.D: An epidemic only affects children, while an endemic illness targets working adults.

explanation: Endemic means a disease is always around at normal, expected levels. An epidemic is when cases suddenly shoot way up above that normal baseline!

question: In an emergency, why do people in a crowd often rush back to the exact entrance they used, ignoring other exits?

options.A: Main entrances are always wider and safer during an emergency.
options.B: Security guards physically block all emergency doors.
options.C: People prefer to walk backward rather than explore new areas.
options.D: Herding behavior makes individuals follow familiar routes and mimic others.

explanation: Under stress, human nature kicks in: we tend to stick to what is familiar and copy whatever the person right next to us is doing.

question: What is one of the biggest challenges facing local disaster agencies in Nigeria?

options.A: Chronic underfunding and a lack of modern rescue equipment
options.B: An excessive surplus of advanced medical helicopters
options.C: Strict adherence to international space agency guidelines
options.D: Too many trained volunteers refusing to work

explanation: That's right. Many local agencies struggle simply because tight budgets make it hard to buy modern gear and keep emergency vehicles running.

question: Why does public stigma surrounding mental illness often hurt patients?

options.A: It improves community support networks for families
options.B: It guarantees immediate admission to a general ward
options.C: It automatically lowers the patient's blood pressure
options.D: It delays seeking professional medical treatment

explanation: Stigma and fear of being judged often cause families to hide loved ones or turn only to traditional options first, delaying the proper medical help they deserve.

question: If a field worker is doing a household survey to find out about maternal deaths without using confusing medical terms, how should they ask?

options.A: Has any female relative suffered from direct obstetric hemorrhage or eclampsia?
options.B: Were there any fatalities resulting from failure of the local primary healthcare board?
options.C: Did any woman in this house die while pregnant, during delivery, or shortly after childbirth?
options.D: Did any woman experience a complete termination of reproductive biomarkers last year?

explanation: Using clear, everyday language about pregnancy timing helps families easily understand and share accurate information without needing a medical degree!

question: How do strict professional hierarchies sometimes hurt patient care?

options.A: They discourage junior staff and nurses from sharing critical patient observations
options.B: They ensure that every single medication is administered twice as fast
options.C: They eliminate all forms of communication errors between departments
options.D: They force patients to pay less money for hospital admission fees

explanation: Spot on! When junior staff or nurses feel intimidated by strict ranks, they might hold back life-saving observations out of fear.

question: Why does milk make it so easy for bacteria to grow quickly?

options.A: It is usually stored in open containers in the market
options.B: It undergoes heavy chemical processing before packaging
options.C: It contains a high concentration of essential nutrients
options.D: It is naturally warm and has a very low pH level

explanation: Spot on! Milk is packed with proteins, fats, and sugars, which makes it a rich food source for microorganisms to feed and multiply on.

question: What physical sign in the neck points toward increased central venous pressure and heart strain?

options.A: Lymph node swelling
options.B: Thyroid gland enlargement
options.C: Jugular venous distension
options.D: Carotid artery pulsation

explanation: When the right side of the heart struggles to pump blood forward, fluid backs up into the venous system, making the neck veins visibly swell or distend. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T13#GNS213_U1_T13_h1)

question: A community nurse gives out insecticide-treated bed nets to prevent malaria. Which part of the epidemiological triangle is this tackling?

options.A: The genetic makeup
options.B: The infectious agent directly
options.C: The environment
options.D: The host immune system

explanation: Great thinking! Bed nets change the environment where humans and mosquitoes meet, keeping the vector away from you.

question: What was the main focus of early home care provided by ancient charitable groups?

options.A: Complex laboratory testing
options.B: Prescription drug management
options.C: Advanced surgical interventions
options.D: Basic hygiene, feeding, and comfort

explanation: Early home nursing was all about supportive care—keeping patients clean, well-fed, and comfortable rather than doing complex medical procedures.

question: What is the recommended daily target for fruit and vegetable portions for adults?

options.A: Exactly ten portions
options.B: Only one single portion
options.C: As many as possible without limit
options.D: At least five portions

explanation: Correct! Aiming for at least five portions a day is a wonderful, simple habit to keep your body healthy and strong.

question: Which nursing action is a great example of 'validating' a patient during an emotional crisis?

options.A: Acknowledging and accepting the reality of the patient's emotional pain
options.B: Telling the patient that their worries are completely irrational
options.C: Insisting that the patient stop crying and focus on paperwork
options.D: Changing the subject immediately to something more cheerful

explanation: Exactly. Validation means letting the patient know: 'I see your pain, I hear you, and your feelings make sense.' It builds instant trust.

question: How do antibodies cause too much hormone to be released in conditions like Graves' disease?

options.A: By mimicking normal regulatory hormones and over-activating receptors
options.B: By blocking hormone breakdown enzymes in the bloodstream
options.C: By shrinking the target gland until it releases stored hormones
options.D: By destroying the pituitary gland to stop feedback loops

explanation: Think of these rogue antibodies as imposters that pretend to be the body's natural signaling messengers, tricking the gland into working overtime. You're doing brilliantly! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h2)

question: What should a nursing team do during the 'Study' phase of a PDSA cycle?

options.A: Purchase new equipment for every unit in the entire hospital
options.B: Compare the actual results to their original predictions and analyze what happened
options.C: Write a formal disciplinary warning for staff who failed to follow instructions
options.D: Design a brand new aim statement from scratch

explanation: Spot on! The Study phase is all about looking at your data and figuring out why the test turned out the way it did.

question: How does a harsh blame culture negatively affect quality assurance efforts?

options.A: It causes patients to leave the hospital against medical advice
options.B: It drives staff to hide mistakes rather than report them for team learning
options.C: It speeds up the process of patient discharge too much
options.D: It forces the hospital to buy more expensive medical drugs

explanation: When people are afraid of harsh punishments, mistakes get swept under the rug. An open, supportive culture helps us learn and grow instead!

question: What is the main job of FSH and LH in the female reproductive cycle?

options.A: To stimulate the ovaries to mature eggs and produce hormones
options.B: To maintain high blood pressure during the luteal phase
options.C: To prevent the hypothalamus from releasing GnRH too quickly
options.D: To directly cause the daily shedding of the uterine lining

explanation: FSH and LH are key messengers from the pituitary gland that talk directly to the ovaries to help eggs grow and make hormones.

question: How does emergency nursing usually feel different from working on a quiet regular ward?

options.A: Ward nursing requires more physical endurance than emergencies
options.B: Emergency nurses work completely independently without a team
options.C: Ward nurses never have to make quick clinical decisions
options.D: Emergency nursing deals with sudden patient surges and limited initial data

explanation: Exactly! ER nursing keeps you on your toes because patients rush in unexpectedly, often before you have their full medical history. Exciting stuff!

question: What is the primary goal of public information during a disaster?

options.A: To generate revenue for local agencies
options.B: To save lives and reduce panic
options.C: To test new telecommunication networks
options.D: To document property damage for insurance

explanation: Clear information prevents chaos and helps people take quick safety measures to protect themselves. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T9#GNS315_U5_T9_h1)

question: A nurse notices that teenagers avoid the clinic because staff members gossip. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Report all visiting teenagers to local religious leaders
options.B: Refuse to treat anyone under the age of eighteen
options.C: Train staff on confidentiality and non-judgmental attitudes
options.D: Close the adolescent clinic and open an adult-only wing

explanation: Exactly right! Building trust through strict confidentiality and a welcoming, non-judgmental attitude is key to helping teens feel safe at the clinic.

question: Which of these is NOT a common reason why nurses resist clinical change?

options.A: Excitement about learning too many new computer systems at once
options.B: Skepticism because past projects failed
options.C: Fear of a heavier workload during busy shifts
options.D: Comfort with familiar, everyday routines

explanation: Well done! Nurses rarely resist change because they are 'too excited' about computers. Resistance usually comes from pure fatigue, fear, and burnout.

question: What is the main goal of patient safety in healthcare?

options.A: To eliminate the cost of hospital stays
options.B: To ensure doctors make all clinical choices
options.C: To speed up the hospital discharge process
options.D: To prevent accidental harm to patients

explanation: Patient safety is all about keeping patients protected from accidental injury or harm while they are receiving care from us. You've got this!

question: A nurse notices a patient's blood pressure dropping fast after surgery but waits hours to tell the doctor. What went wrong here?

options.A: Violating patient confidentiality during shift handoff
options.B: Failure to monitor and report critical changes promptly
options.C: Failing to purchase individual liability insurance
options.D: Inappropriate use of electronic health record templates

explanation: Catching changes is only half the job—reporting them quickly to the medical team is vital to keeping patients safe and avoiding liability.

question: In nursing, what is a 'fomite'?

options.A: An inanimate object that harbors germs
options.B: A chemical used to clean wounds
options.C: A type of resistant bacterium
options.D: An insect that carries disease

explanation: You nailed it! Fomites are non-living items like BP cuffs, tables, or stethoscopes that can pass germs from one person to another.

question: What term describes an infant's inborn, natural mood and emotional reactivity?

options.A: Psyche
options.B: Consciousness
options.C: Delusion
options.D: Temperament

explanation: Temperament refers to the biologically rooted behavioral and emotional traits that babies are born with. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T8#GNS314_U1_T8_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of debriefing sessions for rescue personnel after an operation?

options.A: To punish team members who made minor mistakes during the rescue
options.B: To process emotional experiences and access mental health support
options.C: To calculate financial overtime pay and distribute hazard allowances
options.D: To conduct written examinations on disaster rescue theory

explanation: You've got this! Debriefings give rescue workers a safe space to talk through the heavy stress and trauma they witnessed on the job.

question: In patient safety, what do we call a 'slip' during a procedure?

options.A: An intentional choice to ignore hospital policy
options.B: A failure to diagnose a patient properly on admission
options.C: An error of execution where the physical action fails
options.D: A complete lack of clinical knowledge about a disease

explanation: A slip happens when you know what to do in your head, but your hands briefly mess up the physical step—like hitting the wrong infusion button by accident. It happens to the best of us!

question: A cancer patient on chemotherapy develops a fever and oral thrush. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: The chemotherapy drug caused an allergic reaction on the skin.
options.B: The cancer cells mutated into a bacterial infection.
options.C: The treatment suppressed the immune system, allowing a fungus to overgrow.
options.D: The patient ate too much sugar before coming to the hospital.

explanation: Exactly! Chemo lowers white blood cells, giving everyday germs and fungi like thrush an easy chance to take over.

question: What is one of the most damaging consequences of child marriage on a young girl?

options.A: Termination of formal education and increased health risks
options.B: Enhanced career opportunities in urban areas
options.C: Guaranteed immunity from common infectious diseases
options.D: Immediate financial independence and high social status

explanation: Child marriage abruptly stops a girl's schooling and places her developing body at serious risk during early pregnancy. Education is such a powerful shield for them!

question: Where does the ductus venosus send most of its blood?

options.A: Into the left ventricle
options.B: Into the umbilical arteries
options.C: Into the inferior vena cava
options.D: Directly to the pulmonary trunk

explanation: The ductus venosus acts as a shortcut, routing umbilical blood past the liver to empty right into the inferior vena cava. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h2)

question: In healthcare, what are rates of hospital-acquired bed sores (pressure ulcers) commonly used as?

options.A: Patient financial statements
options.B: Clinical quality indicators
options.C: Hospital architectural blueprints
options.D: Staff disciplinary records

explanation: Exactly. Adverse events like pressure ulcers are tracked closely as indicators to measure just how safe and effective nursing care is in a facility.

question: Why is checking for an intact hymen an unreliable way to judge someone's sexual history?

options.A: It is absent in more than half of all healthy females at birth.
options.B: It disappears completely in all females prior to puberty.
options.C: It can be stretched or torn by non-sexual activities like exercise.
options.D: It regenerates rapidly after any form of physical trauma.

explanation: Important clinical point! Everyday activities like sports, stretching, or using tampons can alter the hymen without any sexual contact.

question: A nurse is feeling very anxious after a traumatic patient incident on the ward. Where should they turn for immediate, supportive help from fellow health workers?

options.A: The public relations department for media statements
options.B: The legal department for liability review
options.C: A hospital-sponsored peer support team
options.D: The billing office for patient records

explanation: Peer support teams are specially trained to offer a comforting shoulder and an empathetic ear when ward incidents shake your confidence.

question: A patient living in severe poverty with no stable shelter comes in with heavy anxiety. What is likely driving this?

options.A: An acute reaction to a rare genetic blood disorder
options.B: An excess intake of heavy metals found in tap water
options.C: Chronic toxic stress from daily survival struggles
options.D: A sudden allergy to standard hospital room bedding

explanation: Spot on. Constant worry about where to sleep or find food puts the brain and body under massive, ongoing stress, which heavily fuels anxiety.

question: What is an important duty for a nurse after a client joins a workshop?

options.A: Monitoring if the work stress is affecting the client's mental health
options.B: Manufacturing the goods alongside the clients every afternoon
options.C: Setting the daily market prices for the workshop products
options.D: Managing the financial bank accounts of mulberry farms

explanation: Nurses watch closely for any signs of burnout or relapse to make sure the work remains healing rather than harmful. Proud of your progress!

question: Why does the actual amount of oxygen (FiO2) a patient receives from a nasal cannula vary from person to person?

options.A: Different hospitals calibrate their wall oxygen outlets to different pressures
options.B: It depends on the patient's breathing rate and depth, which mixes room air with the oxygen
options.C: Patients absorb oxygen at different speeds through their skin
options.D: The plastic tubing stretches or shrinks based on the room temperature

explanation: Because a nasal cannula is an open system, patients breathe in regular room air right along with the oxygen. How fast or deep they breathe changes the exact mix!

question: What does a healthy healing wound bed look like when it's doing well?

options.A: Black and hard
options.B: Yellow and stringy
options.C: Bright red and moist
options.D: Pale white and dry

explanation: You're doing great! Healthy healing tissue (granulation tissue) is packed with fresh blood vessels, giving it a bright red, shiny, and moist look that shows healing is well underway.

question: What is the main goal of financial control in healthcare management?

options.A: To reduce the number of working nursing shifts
options.B: To increase the personal salaries of hospital executives
options.C: To monitor, evaluate, and direct financial resources efficiently
options.D: To eliminate all spending on patient care equipment

explanation: Financial control simply means managing and directing funds properly so the hospital or clinic can run smoothly and keep patients safe.

question: In a drug trial, why do researchers use 'blinding' (hiding who gets the real drug or a fake sugar pill)?

options.A: To make the computer software run faster
options.B: To prove the theoretical construct is correct
options.C: To make sure everyone drops out at the same time
options.D: To stop people's expectations from messing up the results

explanation: If patients or nurses know who got the real medicine, they might act differently or judge results with bias. Blinding keeps everything fair and honest!

question: Why should nurses check and document what is left on a patient's meal tray rather than just taking it away?

options.A: To speed up the collection of dirty kitchen dishes
options.B: To calculate the precise cost of hospital food items
options.C: To ensure accurate tracking of actual calories consumed
options.D: To prevent patients from sharing food with visitors

explanation: An empty tray doesn't always mean the patient ate the food! Direct observation helps us chart their true nutritional intake accurately.

question: What tiny helper in the small intestine makes oral rehydration solution (ORS) work so well?

options.A: Passive diffusion through stomach fat
options.B: Active protein pump rejection
options.C: Sodium-glucose cotransporters
options.D: Renal tubular reabsorption

explanation: Glucose teams up with sodium to pull water quickly across the gut wall, making ORS a brilliant tool against dehydration.

question: Which of the following is an example of print IEC material?

options.A: Illustrated leaflets and posters
options.B: Radio jingles and community songs
options.C: Traditional dance and town criers
options.D: Live theatrical drama skits

explanation: Print materials rely on visual text and graphics, such as leaflets, flyers, and posters, to convey health messages. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T4#GNS124_U5_T4_h3)

question: What tends to happen when vaccination rates drop too low in a neighborhood or community?

options.A: Innate barriers become stronger to compensate
options.B: Antibody levels in newborn babies increase
options.C: Natural immunity replaces the need for shots
options.D: Outbreaks of vaccine-preventable diseases return

explanation: You got it! When herd immunity dips, preventable diseases find open doors to cause new outbreaks.

question: Why is it clinically necessary to evaluate the male partner during infertility workups?

options.A: Women are rarely the sole cause of delayed conception
options.B: Male factors contribute to nearly half of all couple infertility cases
options.C: Government policies mandate joint fertility screenings
options.D: Male testing is much cheaper and faster than female testing
